# Support table: OpenMP target offload, C11

Status: **provisional**. Generated by compliance/report.py (tools/derive/support_table.py --lang c) from results/matrix_c.jsonl, the committed C oracle audit summary ([oracle-audit-c.md](../../reports/oracle-audit-c.md)) and [claims.yaml](../../catalog/vendor_claims_generic.yaml) (claims about C or C/C++ only; a claim that names a do compound covers its for twin). Scope: OpenMP 5.0, 5.2 and 6.0 atoms of the first slice in C: the C ports of the Fortran programs (offload.engine.c_gen, offload.engine.f2c) and the C-only illegal variants. Toolchains: AFAR, CCE 19, CCE 20, CCE 21 on the MI300A (gfx942) and each one's other GPUs; GCC 16.2 on its other AMD GPUs only (not the MI300A); NVHPC 25.11, NVHPC 26.9, GCC 16.2 on the A100 (sm_80); -O2, three runs per cell. The CSV has the Fortran table's columns plus `lang` (c here, f90 there).

## Provenance and memory modes

- 18326 cells: 13574 legal-program cells, 638 host+device pattern cells and 4114 illegal-variant cells (program x toolchain x HSA_XNACK).
- Scope: device offload only. A construct that runs on the host and whose result never reaches a target region is out of scope (the section 'Out of scope (host execution)' lists those atoms); host constructs that feed a target region the way codes use them are host+device patterns, reported in their own section and never as an atom's headline result.
- **Headline mode: HSA_XNACK=1 with transparent huge pages** (LC's example job script) for every program. **Copy mode (HSA_XNACK=0)** for 833 of 833 programs: every program (a full two-mode matrix). A copy-mode column reads 'not run' for the others.
- HSA_XNACK=1 run on tuolumne2151 (THP never, started 2026-10-19T06:47:02); HSA_XNACK=0 run on tuolumne1035 (THP always, started 2026-10-21T14:17:02). Of the program x toolchain pairs with both modes, 132 have both rows from one node, 3200 from different nodes and 0 from unrecorded nodes; where the modes of the latter differ, the cells carry a dagger (†).
- **gfx90a (Tioga, AMD Instinct MI250X, a discrete GPU): HSA_XNACK=0 only** (XNACK is not recommended on MI250X), 833 programs on AFAR gfx90a, CCE 19 gfx90a, CCE 20 gfx90a, CCE 21 gfx90a, GCC 16.2 gfx90a, nodes tioga30, tioga35, tioga36, tioga38, tioga39; the same compiler releases with gfx90a as the offload arch (--offload-arch=gfx90a, craype-accel-amd-gfx90a for CCE, -march=gfx90a for GCC's amdgcn offload), the compilers' default ('xnack any') code objects. Each compiler's third column.
- **gfx942 (AMD Instinct MI300X, a discrete GPU): copy memory (HSA_XNACK=0) only**, 833 programs on AFAR MI300X, GCC 16.2 MI300X, nodes k002-004-v2; the same compiler releases with gfx942 as the offload arch. A column of its own after the gfx90a one; it does not enter the portable verdict.
- **gfx950 (AMD Instinct MI350X, a discrete GPU): copy memory (HSA_XNACK=0) only**, 833 programs on AFAR MI350X, GCC 16.2 MI350X, nodes k007-005-v6; the same compiler releases with gfx950 as the offload arch. A column of its own after the gfx90a one; it does not enter the portable verdict.
- **NVIDIA A100 (wingtip, sm_80): NVHPC 25.11, NVHPC 26.9, GCC 16.2**, 833 programs; NVHPC in separate memory (-gpu=mem:separate, the headline mode) and managed memory (-gpu=mem:managed), each mode its own build; -mp=gpu (OpenACC: -acc=gpu) -gpu=cc80 -O2, no OpenMP version option (every version slice compiles with the default); GCC in separate memory only, -foffload=nvptx-none; no unified memory on that node (not applicable). Host wingtip; gcc (GCC) 16.2.0; nvc 25.11-0 64-bit target on x86-64 Linux -tp icelake-server; nvc 26.9-0 64-bit target on x86-64 Linux -tp icelake-server.

CCE 19 accepts -fopenmp-version=60 without a diagnostic but stays at OpenMP 5.1 (_OPENMP 202011). GCC: gcc -fopenmp -foffload=amdgcn-amdhsa -foffload-options=amdgcn-amdhsa=-march=<the GPU's arch> -O2, no version flag. ROCm loaded with CCE: 6.4.3, 7.2.0.
- `OMP_TARGET_OFFLOAD=mandatory` on the primary run; a failing run is repeated without it to tell host fallback from a wrong answer.

## How to read a cell

- **correct on device**: the check passed and the region ran on the device; the evidence column says how strong that is: `construct` (the check depends on the construct), `probe` (a negative probe: the program names an absent item with the present modifier, so the run must end in the runtime's error termination; the cell reads 'error termination as required (negative probe)', and a run that went on reads 'no error termination (negative probe)'; or a compile-output probe: an error directive with at(compilation) whose message must appear as a warning, or whose fatal severity must stop the compile), `copy_mode_only` (the check separates the construct from a no-op only at HSA_XNACK=0; the headline cell says so and carries ◊: the real check is the copy-mode column, or the cell says 'copy-mode check not run'); the categories below have no separating oracle and are never credited as supported.
- **accepted; conforms vacuously** (`hint_only`): the spec lets an implementation ignore the form (a hint, an assertion the program makes, or a bound one-at-a-time execution meets); **implementation-defined** (`implementation_defined`): the spec leaves the behaviour to the implementation; **equivalent to the default (no separable effect)** (`equivalent_default`): by the spec the form is the behaviour without it. The cell reads so when the program compiled and ran cleanly; the spec sentence is in the citation column and in the section 'Atoms without a separating oracle'. Where the program checks what the form requires (e.g. the number of teams within the bounds) a failure reads as a wrong answer.
- **accepted (its oracle is the illegal variant)** (`legality`): the atom's only effect is a compile-time restriction (default(none)); its oracle is the illegal variant in the illegal-variants table.
- **accepted; unverified (an oracle is possible but missing)** (`unverified`): the spec fixes the behaviour and a deterministic check is possible, but the program does not have it (the audit disposition says why).
- **wrong answer (confirmed)**: the atom's oracle is audited valid (a mutant without the construct is killed on at least one toolchain). **wrong answer (oracle unaudited)** / **oracle unaudited**: measured outcome, but no toolchain passes the original program, so the oracle is unaudited; not a confirmed failure.
- **crash: SIGABRT, HSA_XNACK=1 only**: the program aborts in that memory mode only (shown instead of a plain wrong answer).
- **fails in copy mode: needs zero-copy memory**: the program needs HSA_XNACK=1; failing at HSA_XNACK=0 is expected and is not a feature result.
- **Audit dispositions predate the explicit -fopenmp-version=60 run** of AFAR's 6.0 programs, in which AFAR rejected the originals. ## Reproduction gate

Each failing legal cell (a counted rejection, a wrong answer, a crash, a host fallback, a failed probe) carries the reproduction gate's status (offload.engine.gate, results/gate/verdicts.jsonl, and the decisions of catalog/gate_queue.yaml): **confirmed** (its own rerun verdict, or one inherited from a compile-time defect signature), **decided** (a decision; it counts when the decision says counts_as: failure), **unchecked** (the gate did not rerun it), **nondeterministic**, **ours** (a recorded ruling says the failure is our build's), the other verdicts, or **ungated** (no verdict yet). A cell counts as a compiler failure only when confirmed or decided as counting (report.confirmed_failure; the campaign counts of offload.engine.gate.counts keep unchecked rows at their previous outcome, a different question); every other failing cell is listed apart below, and only counted cells (and ungated ones) contradict a support claim. The CSV's last column, `gate`, has the status of every failing cell.

## Portable verdict (correct at HSA_XNACK=0 and 1 and on gfx90a)

The result a user can rely on for portable code (a discrete GPU has separate host and device memory) is **correct in both memory modes**: at HSA_XNACK=1 (unified memory) a missing or wrong map often still gives the right answer, so a mapping error shows only at HSA_XNACK=0. **and on the discrete GPU**, Tioga's MI250X (gfx90a, HSA_XNACK=0, separate HBM): portable = correct on MI300A at HSA_XNACK=1, at HSA_XNACK=0 and on gfx90a. Per toolchain, the legal programs' verdicts: **portable**: correct at HSA_XNACK=0 and at HSA_XNACK=1; **x1_only**: correct at HSA_XNACK=1 only (unified memory); **x0_only**: correct at HSA_XNACK=0 only (copy mode); **neither**: an observed failure in both modes (rejected, wrong answer, crash, host fallback, a probe that did not terminate, or a presence check failing at HSA_XNACK=1); **x0_fail_x1_unverified**: failed at HSA_XNACK=0; HSA_XNACK=1 not verifiable (nothing observable there, or a copy_mode_only program whose HSA_XNACK=1 check skips what the copy mode tests); **x1_fail_x0_unverified**: failed at HSA_XNACK=1; HSA_XNACK=0 not verifiable; **requirement_refused**: the runtime refuses a requires directive in one mode (supporting a requirement is implementation defined, 5.2 §8.2): a conforming refusal, not a failure; **not_verifiable**: neither mode gives an observable verdict (unobservable, accepted and ignored, no oracle, unverified, harness error, a rejection not counted); **needs_zero_copy**: the program needs zero-copy memory (HSA_XNACK=1) by design; not a portability result; **x0_not_run**: no HSA_XNACK=0 run; **gfx942_only**: correct in both MI300A modes, an observed failure on the discrete gfx90a (MI250X); **gfx90a_unverified**: correct in both MI300A modes; the gfx90a cell gives no verdict (unobservable, ignored, harness error, ...); **gfx90a_not_run**: correct in both MI300A modes; no gfx90a run.

## Portable verdict, NVIDIA (separate and managed memory)

NVHPC 25.11, NVHPC 26.9, GCC 16.2 on an NVIDIA A100 (wingtip, sm_80): the headline mode is separate memory (-gpu=mem:separate, the compiler's default: separate host and device copies, the discrete-GPU mode); managed memory (-gpu=mem:managed) puts dynamically allocated data in CUDA managed memory. Unified memory (-gpu=mem:unified) is not applicable on this machine (no HMM: the runtime refuses to start). Portable = correct in both modes. Per toolchain, the legal programs' verdicts: **portable**: correct in separate and in managed memory; **x1_only**: correct in managed memory only; **x0_only**: correct in separate memory only; **neither**: an observed failure in both modes; **x0_fail_x1_unverified**: failed in separate memory; managed not verifiable; **x1_fail_x0_unverified**: failed in managed memory; separate not verifiable; **not_verifiable**: neither mode gives an observable verdict; **needs_zero_copy**: the program needs zero-copy memory (unified memory, which wingtip does not have) by design; **managed_unverified**: correct in separate memory; the managed-memory cell is not verifiable (managed_shares_storage); **managed_not_run**: no managed-memory run; **one_mode_correct**: correct in the one memory mode the toolchain runs; **one_mode_failure**: an observed failure in the one memory mode the toolchain runs.

## Memory-mode differences

Legal programs (device and host+device) whose outcome differs between HSA_XNACK=1 and HSA_XNACK=0 on a toolchain, with the class of the difference (catalog/mode_differences.yaml): **copy_mode_failure**: correct at HSA_XNACK=1, wrong at 0, and the program's mapping is conforming (it would be correct with separate host and device memory): a compiler copy-mode failure, with a finding; **unified_memory_failure**: correct at HSA_XNACK=0, wrong at 1: a failure specific to unified memory; **needs_unified_memory**: the program requires unified memory by design (requires unified_shared_memory or self_maps, the self map-type modifier): failing or refusing to run at HSA_XNACK=0 is not a portability result; **requirement_refused**: the runtime refuses a requires directive at HSA_XNACK=0 and terminates before the region (supporting a requirement is implementation defined, 5.2 §8.2): conforming, not a wrong answer; **both_wrong**: wrong in both modes, in different ways: not a portability result; **no_finding_yet**: a difference between the modes that no finding explains yet: shown in the table and not counted as a compiler failure; **x1_oracle_blind**: the program's check runs only in copy mode (its HSA_XNACK=1 cell reads correct with copy-mode evidence, which checks nothing the mode hides) and a copy-independent check (tools/campaigns/presence_x1.py, the reproducer) shows the compiler wrong at HSA_XNACK=1 too: a failure in both modes, not a copy-mode failure; **unclassified**: no entry yet.

## Memory-mode differences, NVIDIA (separate versus managed)

Legal programs whose NVHPC outcome differs between separate and managed memory, with the class of the difference (catalog/mode_differences.yaml nvhpc_entries): **separate_failure**: correct in managed memory, wrong in separate memory, the program's mapping conforming: a compiler failure with separate host and device memory (the copy-mode failure), with a finding; **managed_failure**: correct in separate memory, wrong in managed memory: a failure specific to managed memory, with a finding; **both_wrong**: wrong in both modes, in different ways: not a portability result; **needs_unified_memory**: the program requires unified memory by design (requires unified_shared_memory, self_maps): failing without it is not a portability result; **requirement_refused**: the runtime or compiler refuses a requires directive in one mode (supporting a requirement is implementation defined): conforming; **intermittent**: a failure that shows in one mode by chance (a race or a flaky run), not the mode; **not_verifiable**: neither cell gives a verdict the other contradicts (unobservable, ignored or a harness error on one side): not a portability result; **managed_shares_storage**: a copy_mode_only program whose shared-memory probe is local data (separate in managed memory) while its checked arrays are allocatable (managed memory: the device shares their storage, which the spec allows): the copy-semantics check says nothing in managed memory; rerun with the probe on the heap it passes (tools/campaigns/nvhpc_managed_probe.py); **unclassified**: no entry yet.

None.

## gfx90a (MI250X) versus gfx942 (MI300A) copy mode

Both run with separate host and device memory (HSA_XNACK=0); the MI250X is a discrete GPU (its own HBM), the MI300A an APU whose copy mode emulates one. Legal programs (device and host+device) whose gfx90a outcome differs from the MI300A copy-mode outcome: 0 of 2584 compared cells, with the class of the difference (catalog/mode_differences.yaml, arch_entries): **gfx90a_failure**: correct on MI300A, wrong on gfx90a, the program's mapping is conforming: a compiler or runtime failure specific to gfx90a (or to the discrete GPU), with a finding; **x0_emulation_gap**: correct at HSA_XNACK=0 on MI300A, wrong on the discrete gfx90a because something reaches device code without a map that the APU's copy mode still makes accessible: the compiler fails to map it (a mapping failure HSA_XNACK=0 on MI300A hides), with a finding; **gfx942_failure**: wrong at HSA_XNACK=0 on MI300A, correct on gfx90a: a failure specific to the MI300A (APU) copy mode, with a finding; **both_wrong**: wrong on both GPUs, in different ways: not a portability result; **needs_unified_memory**: the program requires unified memory by design; failing or refusing without it is not a portability result; **requirement_refused**: the runtime refuses a requires directive on one GPU (supporting a requirement is implementation defined, 5.2 §8.2): conforming; **no_finding_yet**: a difference between the GPUs that no finding explains yet: shown in the table and not counted as a compiler failure; **intermittent**: a failure the finding shows to be intermittent (a race): it showed in one cell and not in the other by chance; the same program fails on both GPUs in other runs; **not_verifiable**: neither cell gives a verdict the other contradicts (e.g. unobservable on one GPU, ignored or a harness error on the other): not a portability result; **unclassified**: no entry yet.

None.

## Presence checks at HSA_XNACK=1

A copy_mode_only program skips its checks under unified memory, so its HSA_XNACK=1 cell is no evidence. Presence (omp_target_is_present) is defined in both modes, so tools/campaigns/presence_x1.py ran each program with only its presence checks unguarded at HSA_XNACK=1 (tests/data/presence_x1_summary.json). A failure there makes the cell not portable (the portable verdict counts it as an HSA_XNACK=1 failure).

| outcome | AFAR | CCE 19 | CCE 20 | CCE 21 | GCC 16.2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| accepted_ignored | 0 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| correct_on_device | 0 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 0 |

## Vendor claims versus measurements

All claims are **provisional** and cited in [claims.yaml](../../catalog/vendor_claims_generic.yaml). A claim covers an atom by name or pattern; a release-level (general) claim applies only where no specific claim for that toolchain covers the atom. Comparison rules: `supported` is contradicted by rejected, ignored, fell back, wrong answer or crash; `unsupported` by correct on device (or, for a compile-error claim, by anything but rejection); `partial` only when the vendor says the form is accepted and it is rejected. Cells that cannot separate the construct (no oracle: hint only, implementation-defined, equivalent default; legality; unverified; unobservable) never contradict a claim, except that a crash of such an atom does (a crash needs no oracle), and they never count as support; zero-copy programs in copy mode and illegal variants are not compared. Both memory modes are compared where both ran.

## OpenMP 5.0: legal programs, one row per atom

◊ = copy_mode_only: the check separates the construct from a no-op only in copy mode, so the cell's real check is its copy-mode column. † = the two modes differ for that toolchain and their rows ran on different (or unrecorded) nodes, so the node may explain the difference as well as the memory mode.
omp_vv columns (second source, unaudited): narrow omp_vv tests that use the atom (at most one base clause), passes / fails by exit code, each test read at HSA_XNACK=1 or, when its result depends on copy semantics, at HSA_XNACK=0; blank when no narrow test uses the atom.

◊ = copy_mode_only: the check separates the construct from a no-op only in copy mode, so the cell's real check is its copy-mode column. † = the two modes differ for that toolchain and their rows ran on different (or unrecorded) nodes, so the node may explain the difference as well as the memory mode.
omp_vv columns (second source, unaudited): narrow omp_vv tests that use the atom (at most one base clause), passes / fails by exit code, each test read at HSA_XNACK=1 or, when its result depends on copy semantics, at HSA_XNACK=0; blank when no narrow test uses the atom.

## Atoms without a separating oracle

No single run can tell these forms from their absence, and the spec says why (catalog/omp/no_oracle.yaml; every sentence is checked against the spec text). Their cells read as the category, never as support; a rejection or a wrong answer keeps its outcome.

| version | atom | category | spec basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.0 | `clause.aligned` | accepted; conforms vacuously | OpenMP 5.0 §2.9.3.1, p.112: "The aligned clause declares that the location of each list item is aligned to the number of bytes expressed in the optional parameter of the aligned clause." |
| 5.0 | `clause.aligned.alignment` | accepted; conforms vacuously | OpenMP 5.0 §2.9.3.1, p.112: "The aligned clause declares that the location of each list item is aligned to the number of bytes expressed in the optional parameter of the aligned clause." |
| 5.0 | `clause.defaultmap.default` | equivalent to the default (no separable effect) | OpenMP 5.0 §2.19.7.2, p.325: "If implicit-behavior is default, then the clause has no effect for the variables in the category specified by variable-category." |
| 5.0 | `clause.device.device_num` | equivalent to the default (no separable effect) | OpenMP 5.0 §2.12.5, p.172: "If device-modifier does not appear in the clause, the behavior of the clause is as if device-modifier is device_num." |

## Host+device patterns (not headline results)

Host constructs that feed a target region the way codes use them (an exception to the device-offload scope), one program per pattern (id ending in -hostdev). Each is judged on its device result (the check and ran_on_host of the device region); it is not the atom's oracle (no mutation audit) and never counts as the atom's support. The atom's headline is its device-only program in the tables above.

## Out of scope (host execution)

Atoms whose construct of interest runs only on the host, or whose effect never reaches a target region: not device offload, so they have no program, no cell and no verdict here (catalog/omp/out_of_scope.yaml; each sentence is checked against the spec text).

| version | atom | reason | spec |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.0 | `clause.copyin` | copyin copies the primary thread's threadprivate value into the threadprivate copies of a parallel team; the effect of an access to a threadprivate variable in a target region is unspecified, so the clause has a defined effect only in a host parallel region, and that effect never reaches a target region (6.0 also allows copyin on a target compound, where the same restriction leaves it unspecified) | OpenMP 5.0 §2.12.5, p.174: "The effect of an access to a threadprivate variable in a target region is unspecified." |
| 5.0 | `clause.device_type.host` | device_type(host) on declare target makes only a host version of the procedure available: the procedure can be called only on the host and never in a target region (its program called it on the host), so there is no device behaviour to judge | OpenMP 5.0 §2.12.7, p.182: "If host is specified only a host version of the procedure is made available." |
| 5.2 | `clause.copyin` | copyin copies the primary thread's threadprivate value into the threadprivate copies of a parallel team; the effect of an access to a threadprivate variable in a target region is unspecified, so the clause has a defined effect only in a host parallel region, and that effect never reaches a target region (6.0 also allows copyin on a target compound, where the same restriction leaves it unspecified) | OpenMP 5.2 §13.8, p.286: "The effect of an access to a threadprivate variable in a target region is unspecified." |
| 5.2 | `clause.device_type.host` | device_type(host) on declare target makes only a host version of the procedure available: the procedure can be called only on the host and never in a target region (its program called it on the host), so there is no device behaviour to judge | OpenMP 5.2 §13.1, p.275: "If host is specified then only a host device version of the procedure or variable is made available." |
| 6.0 | `clause.copyin` | copyin copies the primary thread's threadprivate value into the threadprivate copies of a parallel team; the effect of an access to a threadprivate variable in a target region is unspecified, so the clause has a defined effect only in a host parallel region, and that effect never reaches a target region (6.0 also allows copyin on a target compound, where the same restriction leaves it unspecified) | OpenMP 6.0 §15.8, p.462: "The effect of an access to a threadprivate variable in a target region is unspecified." |

## Results that depend on provisional rules

Nothing in the catalog has been reviewed by the maintainer yet, so every result depends on provisional data:

- **Every legal cell** depends on its atom's clause-grammar entry ([clauses.yaml](../../catalog/omp/clauses.yaml): {'provisional': 56} of 56 clauses) and on the generator's reading of it.
- **Every illegal-variant cell** depends on the one rule it violates ([rules.yaml](../../catalog/omp/rules.yaml): {'provisional': 189} of 189 rules; 187 rule versions exercised here).
- **Spec overrides** of the TableGen skeleton (catalog/omp/spec_overrides.yaml: {'provisional': 111} of 111) decide whether a clause is allowed on a directive at 5.0, 5.2 or 6.0. ## Corpus baseline (omp_vv C target tests)

5440 results (340 files x toolchain x memory mode run). Every test ran in both modes (HSA_XNACK=1 with the matrix run on tuolumne2151; HSA_XNACK=1 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1032 (2026-10-24T09:18:07); HSA_XNACK=1 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1032 (2026-10-24T09:20:45); HSA_XNACK=1 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1032 (2026-10-24T09:23:07); HSA_XNACK=1 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1032 (2026-10-24T09:25:31); HSA_XNACK=0 with the matrix run on tuolumne1035; HSA_XNACK=0 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1029 (2026-10-24T09:18:13); HSA_XNACK=0 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1029 (2026-10-24T09:20:51); HSA_XNACK=0 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1029 (2026-10-24T09:23:16); HSA_XNACK=0 rows of 340 tests rerun on tuolumne1029 (2026-10-24T09:25:42)). Each test is compiled with the compiler's default OpenMP version (5.1) when its spec directory is 4.5, 5.0 or 5.1, with -fopenmp-version= its directory for 5.2 and 6.0, and with the suite's -I ompvv -lm, run once under OMP_TARGET_OFFLOAD=mandatory. Pass criterion: exit code 0; the tests are **unaudited** (their self-checks were not mutation-tested).
